Smart plugs are the easiest entry point into home automation. Plug in a lamp, a coffee maker, or a fan, and suddenly you can control them from your phone, set schedules, or use voice commands. But which budget smart plug should you buy? We compare the Kasa Smart Plug HS103P4 4-Pack and the Amazon Basics Smart Plug 2-Pack to find out.

Quick Verdict

Buy the Kasa Smart Plug HS103P4 4-pack if: You want universal compatibility. The Kasa works with Alexa, Google Home, and IFTTT, giving you the freedom to switch ecosystems. It also packs scheduling, timer, and away mode into a compact design that won't block adjacent outlets. At $8.70 per plug, the Kasa is the best all-around smart plug value on Amazon.

Buy the Amazon Basics Smart Plug if: You're 100% Alexa-only and don't plan to switch. The Amazon Basics plug works exclusively with Alexa — no Google Home, no IFTTT, no Matter. At $7.50 per plug, it's cheap but limited.

Our pick: The Kasa HS103P4 4-Pack. The per-plug cost is marginally higher, but the broader ecosystem support and feature set make it the smarter long-term investment for any smart home.

TP-Link's Kasa brand has been the gold standard for budget smart home gear for years, and the HS103 is proof. This 4-pack is one of Amazon's best-selling smart plug bundles, with hundreds of thousands of reviews and a 4.4+ star rating that reflects real-world reliability.

Amazon Basics Smart Plug (2-Pack)

$15.00 ($7.50/plug) on Amazon

Amazon Basics entered the smart plug game a few years back with a simple proposition: the cheapest way to get voice control for your home. At $15 for a 2-pack, it delivers on that promise.

These plugs work exclusively with Alexa — that's Amazon's whole play. You plug it in, say "Alexa, discover devices," and you're up and running. The Amazon Alexa app handles scheduling, timers, and remote control. It's dead simple for anyone already living in Amazon's ecosystem.

The build quality is decent — not premium but functional. The plugs are slightly bulkier than the Kasa, and they can block adjacent outlets depending on your receptacle spacing. There's also no energy monitoring, no away mode randomization, and no IFTTT support. It does what it says on the box, and nothing more.

Key specs: 2 plugs total, Alexa-only, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, no hub required, scheduling and timers via Alexa app, no IFTTT/Google support.

Ecosystem Lock-In Is the Real Cost

The $1.20 per plug savings on the Amazon Basics seems appealing until you realize what you're giving up. Here's why ecosystem flexibility matters more than most people think:

You might switch assistants. Maybe you start with Alexa but later buy a Google Nest Hub or prefer the Google Assistant's search capabilities. With Kasa, you switch apps — no hardware swap needed. With Amazon Basics, you're buying all new plugs.

Automation opens up with IFTTT. IFTTT (If This Then That) lets you connect your smart plugs to thousands of other services. You can have your Kasa plug turn on a lamp when your phone's GPS detects you're 5 minutes from home, or flash the lights when your Ring doorbell rings. Amazon Basics plugs can't do any of this.

Away mode is a security feature. The Kasa's away mode randomly turns lights on and off to simulate occupancy. It's a basic but effective deterrent when you're on vacation. The Amazon Basics plug simply offers on/off scheduling — no randomization.

💡 Pro tip: If you're outfitting a whole house, the Kasa 4-pack is the start. Their ecosystem expands with smart switches, bulbs, and power strips that all work within the same Kasa app. It's a cohesive smart home platform, not just a one-trick pony.

When Amazon Basics Makes Sense

The Amazon Basics Smart Plug is a fine product for its target audience: people who only use Alexa and want the absolute cheapest way to voice-control a few devices. If you have an Echo in every room and no plans to ever use Google Home, the $7.50/plug price is genuinely good value.

But those savings disappear if you ever decide to switch assistants. The resale value of an Amazon Basics plug is essentially zero.

The Bottom Line

The Kasa Smart Plug HS103P4 4-Pack is the clear winner here. At $8.70 per plug, you're paying a modest premium for dramatically more functionality: Google Home compatibility, IFTTT automation, away mode, a more compact design, and no ecosystem lock-in.

Smart home gear is a long-term investment. The extra $1.20 per plug for the Kasa is easily justified by the flexibility it gives you down the road. Don't save a few dollars now only to replace everything later.
